components.name: Left Nav Pane
components.description: Rebuilt this pass on Fluent 2's own NavDrawer/NavDrawerHeader/NavDrawerBody/NavItem/Hamburger primitives, replacing the prior hand-rolled two-tier top bar (a plain <nav> of <Link>s under a brand strip). Inline (persistent, 320px) at 1024px and up; overlay (closed by default, floats above content) below it, switched by a window.matchMedia listener. Each item carries a bundleIcon'd Fluent icon that swaps outline-to-filled on the active route, plus the Hungarian label. Selected state is Fluent's native treatment (bold white text, tinted background, inset left accent bar) re-pinned to the shell palette instead of Fluent's brand green. The prior per-item 'tint' marking two secondary routes was dropped — a top-bar-specific highlight with no meaning once items are full-width vertical rows.

components.name: Page Backdrop
components.description: The full-bleed dark/purple gradient every page's outer wrapper applies via the shared usePageBackdropStyles hook (src/styles/shell.ts) — one hook, one place, not re-declared per page. min-height: 100dvh ensures it fills the content column's height even on short pages; the column is now narrower than the viewport whenever the nav pane is open, which the gradient's percentage-based positions absorb with no per-page change.
components.css: .ds-page-backdrop { min-height: 100dvh; background-color: #1b1430; background-image: radial-gradient(ellipse 900px 700px at 8% 95%, #5b21b6 0%, #312e81 45%, transparent 72%), radial-gradient(ellipse 800px 650px at 95% 2%, #9333ea 0%, #241a3f 50%, transparent 75%); background-repeat: no-repeat; }

narrative.overview: Zero Gluten runs inside a dark navy/indigo chrome over a purple gradient backdrop — a register borrowed, user-pinned, from an unrelated enterprise dashboard reference. The product itself hasn't changed across either shell pass: it's still a plain-spoken kitchen companion, read one-handed, sometimes in a dim kitchen or a shop. Every real task — ingredient lists, shopping checkboxes, the cook-today answer — still lives on the same white, elevated cards this system built before any of the dark chrome existed; only the chrome and the page background around those cards went dark and colorful. This pass rebuilt the chrome itself: the nav moved from a two-tier top bar to a collapsible left pane, built on Fluent 2's own NavDrawer primitives rather than hand-rolled links. The visual identity carries over unchanged — same hex, same two-tier brand/link split, just rotated from horizontal to vertical — but the nav is now a distinct, Fluent-native component: real keyboard navigation, a native selected-state treatment, and a built-in responsive collapse to an overlay on narrow viewports. The theme architecture itself stayed light (FluentProvider on zeroGlutenTheme, unchanged): the dark/purple treatment is hand-pinned hex applied only to chrome and page backgrounds, never inside a card, so every already-proven component — including the new nav, once its own default theme-driven background was overridden — kept its exact in-card contrast with zero re-verification needed.
keyCharacteristics: Theme architecture is deliberately split: Fluent stays on the light theme; dark/purple is hand-pinned hex on chrome and backdrop only, never inside a card.

The left nav is a real Fluent 2 component (NavDrawer/NavItem/Hamburger), not a styled list of links — it inherits the shell palette via per-slot className overrides, not Fluent's own default theme-driven styling.
Purple/indigo is the chrome/world color; rosemary green is demoted, not removed — it keeps its prior meaning inside cards.
Left-edge status stripes, not top strips, on Catalog and Today's cards.

Off-card text is a first-class concern: several real content elements, including the nav's own brand label and links, sit directly on the dark backdrop and are individually checked against the rendered page, not assumed safe.
Bundle size unaffected — no new dependency beyond the already-installed Fluent package; pure hex constants and CSS gradients.

rules.name: The Always-Flagged Rule
rules.body: The gluten-risk-ingredient signal is reserved exclusively for that one meaning, on every page, regardless of color or backdrop. Never reuse it for anything else, never ship a screen that lists a flaggable ingredient without it. Codified in specs/constitution.md Principle 7.

rules.name: The One Hex, One Place Rule
rules.body: In-card colors stay in src/styles/colors.ts, shell/backdrop colors in src/styles/shellColors.ts, each imported everywhere needed, never re-declared locally.

rules.name: The Left-Border Reversal
rules.body: Left/right decorative card borders are a standing craft-floor ban in general, but meal-type color deliberately renders as a left-edge stripe on Catalog and Today cards, and the nav's selected-item indicator is a 3px inset box-shadow in the same spirit — both earned exceptions, re-pinned to the shell palette. The nest-cards-inside-cards ban is unaffected.

rules.name: The Check-The-Component's-Own-Defaults Rule
rules.body: A library component (NavItem) carries its own default background from the active Fluent theme regardless of what backdrop it's dropped onto — composing it inside a hand-pinned dark surface requires explicitly overriding that default, not just adding new color on top. Caught only by reading the rendered page's computed styles.

dos: Do keep FluentProvider on the light theme — dark/purple styling is chrome-only, hand-pinned hex, never a theme-level switch.
Do check every page's actual rendered output — including a library component's own computed styles — before trusting a written plan's survey.
Do reach for Fluent's own primitives (NavDrawer, NavItem, Hamburger) over hand-rolled nav markup when the library ships one — only the color layer needs re-pinning to the shell palette.
Do keep the gluten-risk color and the three meal-type hues sourced from their one shared module each, regardless of position or backdrop.
Do box genuinely dense content in its own white card rather than recoloring many individual text nodes.
donts: Don't assume a page — or a drop-in component — has no contrast problem because nothing in the diff touched color; verify the real render.
Don't map the gluten-risk signal or any data-series hue to a UI framework's own semantic color token.

Don't carry forward a decorative distinction into a new structure just because it existed before — the old nav's route 'tint' was dropped precisely because the left-pane layout gave it no meaning to preserve.
Don't give every list card treatment by default — Label checklist's flat list is a deliberate exception.
Don't treat this file as a transition snapshot — the left-pane-nav, dark-shell system is the one and only shipped state across all six pages plus the app shell.
